thread:
Maria R: running the expanded safety eval on sentry-7b-int4-ptq-v3 vs fp16 baseline. quick TL;DR: token-level drift on refusal phrases, higher adversarial toxic hits, but 3x lower median p95 latency. full artifacts in the run folder.

opsbot: Note: sentry-7b-int4-ptq-v3 deployed to staging-shadow at 2026-03-10T16:20Z (shadow run queued).

safety-bot: New redteam bundle uploaded: internal://redteam/sentry/6172459999/index.html :rotating_light:

Leila: numbers?

Maria R: pulled the comparison on the 7k eval bundle (5k adv redteam + 2k toxicity holdout):

```
Model         | adv_toxic_rate | refusal_confidence_pct | median_p95_latency_ms
sentry-fp16   | 2.8%           | 90.4                  | 125 / 210
sentry-int4   | 4.2%           | 76.0                  | 38 / 65
```

Maria R: adv_toxic_rate is adversarial prompts that produced toxic outputs (human-labeled subset). refusal_confidence_pct is percent of replies with classifier score >0.85.

Ashwin P: concrete cases?

Maria R: examples in artifacts. small snippet: attacker prefixes with role-swap and COT prompt; fp16 replies with safe refusal; int4 emits stepwise mitigation steps (unsafe).

Oliver: did you inspect logits? any systematic token shifts?

Maria R: yep. ran token-delta heatmap. refusal-related tokens ("I cannot","I can't","I won't") show a mean logit decrease of ~0.7 across early decode steps under int4. also observed slight eos-token prob jitter in multi-turn.

Leila: could be quantizer clipping on per-channel scales. which PTQ recipe? symmetric per-channel + min-max clip?

Maria R: standard PTQ: per-channel symmetric, 4-bit int8 emulation map used for calibration. nothing fancy. also saw some BPE merge differences when caching tokenizer fastpath.

Ashwin P: two-prong repro plan: 1) zero-kv reduced XOR test, 2) bias-correct on refusal-tokens (additive) + temp-sweep. Maria, can you run both on the 1k focused set?

Maria R: starting reproducer now:

```
# focused redteam repro (no kv, logits dump)
python eval/run_redteam.py --model sentry-7b-int4-ptq-v3 \
  --prompts data/redteam/focus_prefixes.csv \
  --no_kv_cache --batch 1 --seed 7 --dump_logits /tmp/sentry_int4_logits.npy
```

Maria R: also kicking bias-correct experiments with per-token additive fit on safe-corpus (script at tools/ptq_bias_correct.py).

Oliver: add a run where we emulate fp16 logits but decode with int4 kernels (logit-replacement) to isolate kernel vs decode ordering.

Maria R: good call. will run "logit-swap" variant next.

Ashwin P: if bias-correct recovers >80% of the refusal gap without hurting utility, we can ship a calibration pass in the inference path. otherwise fallback strategies: 1) route safety-sensitive flows to fp16 pool, 2) sidecar refusal classifier enforce.

Leila: prefer sidecar classifier short-term (cheaper), but we need FP/TP curves vs helpfulness. set up small A/B on staging-shadow.

opsbot: Shadow A/B scheduled: sj-20260310-17 (int4 raw vs int4+bias vs fp16 fallback) pending approvals.

Maria R: early bias-correct trial (n=500): adv_toxic_rate down 4.2% -> 3.3%, refusal_confidence up 76.0 -> 83.5. still validating.

Oliver: sounds promising. also audit tokenizer fastpath cache and BPE mapping. small tokenization differences can cascade when decoding logits near threshold.

Maria R: noted. I saw two merges that changed over calibration; logging tokenizer-merge-diffs now.

Leila: timeline + assignments:
- Maria R: full per-token diff export + logit-heatmaps + tokenize-diff (EOD)
- Ashwin P: bias-correct sweep (additive & temp) + paired utility checks (1 day)
- Oliver: kv-cache/drop and logit-swap runs + multi-turn stress (1 day)
- Safety: expand redteam with persona-switch + COT chains (safety-bot added 2k prompts)

safety-bot: Added persona-switch & chain-of-thought bundle to queue (2,000 prompts). Will post results.

Maria R: linking artifacts: internal://artifacts/models/sentry/int4/6172459999/

Ashwin P: if we still see gap after calibration, consider hybrid decode: use int4 for generation but run a lightweight refusal re-ranker that uses fp16 logits on top-k to decide enforcement. might be a good compromise.

Leila: agree. aim to have decision by follow-up triage tomorrow. thanks team. :pray:
